name: Ts’ui Shu
bio: Ts’ui Shu was a T’ang poet who took his degree in AD 738, according to the chronology of poets in The Jade Mountain.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu’s version in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet’s name as spelled here.

poems.title: A Climb on the Mountain Holiday to the Terrace Whence One Sees the Magician
poems.author: Ts’ui Shu
poems.note: A Poem Sent to Vice-Prefect Liu
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
The Han Emperor Wen bequeathed us this terrace
Which I climb to watch the coming dawn.
Cloudy peaks run northward in the three Chin districts,
And rains are blowing westward through the two Ling valleys.
. . . Who knows but me about the Guard at the Gate,
Or where the Magician of the River Bank is,
Or how to find that magistrate, that poet,
Who was as fond as I am of chrysanthemums and winecups?

poems.title: 九日登望仙台呈劉明府容 (Jiu ri deng wang xian tai cheng liu ming fu rong)
poems.author: Ts’ui Shu
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.text:
漢文皇帝有高臺，此日登臨曙色開。
三晉雲山皆北向，二陵風雨自東來。
關門令尹誰能識，河上仙翁去不回。
且欲近尋彭澤宰，陶然共醉菊花杯。
